#### 1. complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 7  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.397)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8955332)

**Proposed mechanism:** AGBL1 (HGNC:27318) —DISRUPTS→ microtubule dynamics (GO:0007010); TUBB2B (HGNC:11714) —DISRUPTS→ microtubule dynamics (GO:0007010); microtubule dynamics (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ neuronal migration (GO:0001707); neuronal migration (GO:0001707) —LEADS_TO→ complex cortical dysplasia (HP:0002099); neuronal migration (GO:0001707) —LEADS_TO→ other brain malformations (HP:0002100); complex cortical dysplasia (HP:0002099) —LEADS_TO→ MONDO:0014228 phenotype (MONDO:0014228); other brain malformations (HP:0002100) —LEADS_TO→ MONDO:0012399 phenotype (MONDO:0012399). Loss-of-function mutations in AGBL1 and TUBB2B disrupt normal microtubule dynamics, which in turn impairs neuronal migration, leading to the complex cortical dysplasia and other brain malformations characteristic of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in AGBL1 or TUBB2B associated with loss-of-function mechanisms in individuals affected by either disease would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if individuals with MONDO:0014228 consistently lack mutations in these genes or exhibit gain-of-function effects, this hypothesis would be weakened. _(variant: Absence of common loss-of-function variants in AGBL1 and TUBB2B in relevant populations within gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of microtubule dynamics and neuronal migration in these distinct but mechanistically linked conditions could inform therapeutic strategies targeting neuronal development for rare brain malformation syndromes.

#### 2. oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest 24  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.395)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8955332)

**Proposed mechanism:** AGBL1 (HGNC:26817) —DISRUPTS→ cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010); cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ abnormal embryonic development (HP:0001263); TUBA1C (HGNC:11652) —DISRUPTS→ cell division (GO:0051301); cell division (GO:0051301) —LEADS_TO→ oocyte maturation arrest (HP:0030070); cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010) —BINDS→ cell division (GO:0051301). Loss-of-function mutations in AGBL1 disrupt cytoskeletal organization, leading to abnormal embryonic development (Disease A). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TUBA1C disrupt cell division, resulting in oocyte maturation arrest (Disease B). Both cytoskeletal organization and cell division are tightly linked processes, with proper cytoskeletal function being essential for accurate cell division, thus representing a shared mechanistic convergence point.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that AGBL1 and TUBA1C function in completely independent cellular pathways with no downstream interaction or overlap in critical cellular machinery required for cell division and embryonic development. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying the shared mechanistic link between cytoskeletal organization and cell division disruptions caused by mutations in AGBL1 and TUBA1C could pave the way for novel therapeutic strategies targeting these fundamental cellular processes to improve outcomes in both conditions.

**Proposed mechanism:** AGBL1 (HGNC:27800) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal development (GO:0048666); neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ MONDO:0014228 (MONDO:0014228); TUBA4A (HGNC:11676) —DISRUPTS→ cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010); cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ congenital myopathy 26 (MONDO:0979229); neuronal development (GO:0048666) —BINDS→ cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010). Haploinsufficiency of AGBL1 disrupts neuronal development, leading to MONDO:0014228. Simultaneously, haploinsufficiency of TUBA4A disrupts cytoskeletal organization, leading to congenital myopathy 26. These two pathways converge as neuronal development and cytoskeletal organization are intrinsically linked processes.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any observed functional or physical interaction between AGBL1 and TUBA4A pathways in cellular models, or demonstration that mutations in TUBA4A do not impact cytoskeletal organization and neuronal development, or mutations in AGBL1 do not impact neuronal development. _(variant: N/A)_

The convergence is on the shared pathway of cytoskeletal dynamics, critical for neuronal function.

**How to falsify it:** Evidence that AGBL1 and TUBA4A function in completely independent cellular pathways with no downstream overlap in cytoskeletal regulation or neuronal function would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of AGBL1 or TUBA4A that are not associated with either disease would weaken the causal link.)_
